####################################################################################################
Purpose of script: To translate anti-VZV ELISA immunogenicity into continuous protection and compare
vaccination ages and targeted delays, using the semeth VZV model and the Habib et al. Dunning curve
####################################################################################################

# Set up

```{r}
rm(list = ls())
source("../00_pck.R")
source("../00_dirs.R")
source("../fun_mod/fun_venewdata.R")

theme_set(theme_classic() + theme(strip.background = element_blank()))
set.seed(2305)
```

# Define main analyses

The main analysis uses the Dunning logistic model for **all confirmed varicella**,
anti-VZV ELISA, from Supplementary Table 1 of
[Habib et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.vaccine.2021.02.074).
The anti-gE coefficients and the moderate-to-severe square-root model are not used.
The source files are saved alongside this script in `vzv_continuous_protection_sources`.

```{r}
pat_sel <- "vzv"
mod_sel <- "bmv1_semeth_s08_vzv_csi_reg_4.rds"
sim_ndraws <- 1000
sim_vacage <- 38:78
age_ini_sel <- c(38, 45, 52)
age_late <- 52
delay_l <- 1:26
n_birth_week <- 1000

# 42 days matches the paper; 30 days preserves the existing population assumptions.
time_sample <- c(42, 30)

# Concentrations must be anti-VZV ELISA mIU/mL, with compatible assay calibration.
# ELISA alone is not sufficient to establish assay equivalence.
antibody_units <- "mIU/mL"
assay_scale_confirmed <- TRUE

# Separate results from immunogenicity and threshold-based protection.
dir_res <- glue("{dirs$modres}/modresimm_vzv_continuous")
dir.create(dir_res, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Define continuous protection curve

For antibody concentration `a` in mIU/mL, use
`p(a) = plogis(beta0 + beta1 * log10(a))`.
The base-10 implementation reproduces the anti-VZV Dunning curve in Figure 4A
(e.g. approximately 0.20 breakthrough probability at 100 mIU/mL).

`p(a)` is the Dunning model's latent protection probability.
The ten-year disease risk is `lambda * (1 - p(a))` under the study's exposure
conditions. Therefore `1 - disease risk` is **not** the same quantity as `p(a)`.
The article's modelled VE uses the risk at 12.5 mIU/mL (half its 25 mIU/mL
seropositivity cutoff) as the reference; this is separate from your data's cutoff of 50.
No conversion by the ratio of those cutoffs is applied.

```{r}
# Supplementary Table 1, anti-VZV, all confirmed varicella
curve_ref <- tribble(
  ~parameter, ~estimate, ~cilo, ~ciup,
  "lambda",      0.7517,  0.4987,  1.0047,
  "beta0",      -2.2983, -3.3686, -1.2281,
  "beta1",       1.6631,  1.3808,  1.9454
)

# Primary curve: published point estimates.
# Additional curves: marginal-CI corners for sensitivity, NOT joint confidence draws.
# The article does not supply the joint coefficient covariance matrix.
curve_scenarios <- tibble(curve = "published", beta0 = -2.2983, beta1 = 1.6631) %>%
  bind_rows(crossing(beta0 = c(-3.3686, -1.2281), beta1 = c(1.3808, 1.9454)) %>%
              mutate(curve = paste0("sensitivity_", row_number()))) %>%
  mutate(lambda = 0.7517,
         risk_ref = lambda * plogis(-(beta0 + beta1 * log10(12.5))))

fun_protection <- function(a, beta0, beta1) {
  plogis(beta0 + beta1 * log10(a))
}

curve_check <- crossing(antibody = c(25, 100, 750, 1000, 10000), curve_scenarios) %>%
  mutate(protection = fun_protection(antibody, beta0, beta1),
         risk10 = lambda * (1 - protection))
filter(curve_check, curve == "published")
```

# Read in data

```{r}
dat_cov <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$modres}/modresimm_population/dat_cov.rds")) %>%
  filter(pat == pat_sel, mod_best == mod_sel, imm_met_s1 == "elisa") %>%
  distinct()
stopifnot(nrow(dat_cov) == 1)

path_mod <- file.path("/Volumes/ExternalSSD_LABG_Work/_seas_imm_backup/outputs/models", pat_sel, mod_sel)
mod <- readRDS(path_mod)
dat <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$modfit}/datasemeth_brms_vzv_v1_s08.rds"))
stopifnot(all(as.character(dat$imm_met_s1) == "elisa"),
          all(as.character(dat$imm_sero_s1) == "anti_vzv"),
          tolower(mod$family$family) == "gamma")

all_datagapssim <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$modres}/all_datagapssim.rds"))
clu_included <- all_datagapssim %>%
  filter(mod == mod_sel, included == TRUE) %>% pull(clu) %>% str_remove_all(" ")

dat_phase <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$modres}/wbest_phisumm.rds")) %>%
  filter(mod == mod_sel) %>%
  mutate(clu = str_remove_all(as.character(clu), " "),
         min_week = round(((phi_mean - 1 + 26) %% 52) + 1)) %>%
  filter(clu %in% clu_included) %>%
  select(pat, mod_best = mod, clu, min_week) %>% distinct() %>% ungroup()
stopifnot(nrow(dat_phase) > 0, !anyDuplicated(dat_phase$clu), !anyNA(dat_phase$min_week))

# Check response scale: no log/standardisation transformation of the outcome.
lhs <- formula(mod)$formula[[2]]
if (is.call(lhs) && identical(lhs[[1]], as.name("|"))) lhs <- lhs[[2]]
stopifnot(identical(lhs, as.name("imm_val_s1")))

# Confirm compatible units/calibration before producing clinical interpretations.
if (!assay_scale_confirmed) {
  stop("Confirm anti-VZV ELISA mIU/mL and compatible assay calibration, then set assay_scale_confirmed = TRUE.")
}
```

# Obtain immunogenicity predictions

The same fixed covariates and exclusions as `modresimm_population` are retained.
Predictions are regenerated at 42 and 30 days, using the same posterior draw IDs at
both times. `re_formula = NA` retains the previous conditional, zero-random-effect
prediction convention. These are not averages over between-study random effects.

```{r}
# Recover draw IDs from the existing semeth immunogenicity predictions.
imm_files <- list.files(glue("{dirs$modres}/modresimm_population"), full.names = TRUE)
path_imm <- imm_files[str_starts(basename(imm_files),
  fixed(paste0("imm_", str_remove(mod_sel, "[.]rds$"), "_age26to78_draw"))) &
  str_ends(imm_files, "[.]rds$")]
stopifnot(length(path_imm) == 1)
dat_imm_saved <- readRDS(path_imm)
draw_id <- sort(unique(dat_imm_saved$draw))
stopifnot(all(draw_id %in% seq_len(ndraws(mod))))
draw_id <- head(draw_id, sim_ndraws)
rm(dat_imm_saved)

newdat <- map_dfr(time_sample, function(time_x) {
  datcov_x <- dat_cov %>% mutate(time_vl_s1_fixed = time_x)
  fun_venewdat(dat, datcov_x, "reg_4") %>%
    filter(age == datcov_x$age_fixed[[1]]) %>%
    select(-age) %>% crossing(age = sim_vacage) %>%
    filter(str_remove_all(as.character(reg_4), " ") %in% clu_included) %>%
    relocate(age, .after = sex)
})

newdat_key <- newdat %>%
  transmute(clu = str_remove_all(as.character(reg_4), " "), sex, age,
            vac_week_v1, time_vl_s1)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(newdat_key), setequal(newdat_key$clu, dat_phase$clu))
mu <- posterior_epred(mod, newdata = newdat, re_formula = NA, draw_ids = draw_id)
shape <- as_draws_df(mod)$shape[draw_id]
stopifnot(all(is.finite(mu)), all(mu > 0), all(is.finite(shape)), all(shape > 0))

saveRDS(list(newdat = newdat, draw_id = draw_id, mu = mu, shape = shape),
        glue("{dir_res}/imm_semeth_vzv.rds"))
```

# Average protection over the antibody distribution

For each posterior draw, integrate the protection curve over the Gamma antibody
distribution. Do not apply the curve directly to the mean `mu`.
Midpoint Gamma quantiles and interpolation over log mean concentration keep this
step manageable. The numerical check below compares against direct integration.

```{r}
fun_prob <- function(mu_x, shape_x, beta0, beta1, n_quantile = 1024, n_grid = 256) {
  stopifnot(all(mu_x > 0), shape_x > 0)
  log_mu <- seq(log(min(mu_x)) - 1e-8, log(max(mu_x)) + 1e-8, length.out = n_grid)
  # Unit-mean Gamma; scaling by mu gives the distribution for each prediction row.
  antibody_unit <- qgamma((seq_len(n_quantile) - 0.5) / n_quantile,
                         shape = shape_x, rate = shape_x)
  prob_grid <- rowMeans(plogis(beta0 + beta1 *
                        outer(log_mu / log(10), log10(antibody_unit), "+")))
  approx(log_mu, prob_grid, xout = log(mu_x), rule = 2)$y
}

# Check tails and intermediate concentrations against direct quadrature.
check_grid <- crossing(mu = as.numeric(quantile(mu, c(0, .5, 1))),
                       shape = as.numeric(quantile(shape, c(0, .5, 1))),
                       curve_scenarios)
check_grid <- check_grid %>%
  mutate(prob_approx = pmap_dbl(list(mu, shape, beta0, beta1),
                               ~ fun_prob(..1, ..2, ..3, ..4)),
         prob_integral = pmap_dbl(list(mu, shape, beta0, beta1), function(m, sh, b0, b1) {
           integrate(function(u) fun_protection(qgamma(u, shape = sh, rate = sh / m), b0, b1),
                     lower = 0, upper = 1, rel.tol = 1e-7, subdivisions = 1000)$value
         }),
         error = abs(prob_approx - prob_integral))
stopifnot(max(check_grid$error) < 0.0005)
check_grid %>% summarise(max_error = max(error))
```

# Define vaccination scenarios

As before, the targeted period includes the minimum week and the next 12 weeks.
Everyone-later means vaccination at 52 weeks; it is not a uniform delay of `delay`
weeks. All comparisons preserve the same population weights and posterior draws.

```{r}
dat_pop <- dat_phase %>%
  crossing(birth_week = 1:52, sex = c("F", "M"), age_ini = age_ini_sel,
           delay = delay_l, time_vl_s1 = time_sample) %>%
  filter(age_ini + delay <= max(sim_vacage)) %>%
  mutate(n = n_birth_week / 2,
         vac_week_ini = ((birth_week - 1 + age_ini) %% 52) + 1,
         bad_season = ((vac_week_ini - min_week) %% 52) <= 12)

dat_strategy <- bind_rows(
  dat_pop %>% mutate(scenario = "baseline", age = age_ini, vac_week_v1 = vac_week_ini),
  dat_pop %>% mutate(scenario = "later", age = age_late,
                     vac_week_v1 = ((birth_week - 1 + age_late) %% 52) + 1),
  dat_pop %>% mutate(scenario = "targeted", age = age_ini + if_else(bad_season, delay, 0L),
                     vac_week_v1 = ((vac_week_ini - 1 + if_else(bad_season, delay, 0L)) %% 52) + 1)
) %>%
  left_join(newdat_key %>% mutate(pred_row = row_number()),
            by = join_by(clu, sex, age, vac_week_v1, time_vl_s1), relationship = "many-to-one")
stopifnot(!anyNA(dat_strategy$pred_row))

# A sparse weight matrix aggregates predictions without expanding all posterior draws.
strategy_groups <- dat_strategy %>%
  distinct(clu, age_ini, delay, time_vl_s1, scenario) %>% mutate(group_id = row_number())
dat_strategy <- dat_strategy %>%
  left_join(strategy_groups, by = join_by(clu, age_ini, delay, time_vl_s1, scenario)) %>%
  group_by(group_id) %>% mutate(weight = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()
weights <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = dat_strategy$pred_row, j = dat_strategy$group_id,
                               x = dat_strategy$weight,
                               dims = c(nrow(newdat), nrow(strategy_groups)))
stopifnot(all(abs(Matrix::colSums(weights) - 1) < 1e-10))
```

# Estimate population protection

```{r}
sim_draws <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(curve_scenarios)), function(x) {
  curve_x <- curve_scenarios[x, ]
  message(glue("Continuous VZV protection: {curve_x$curve}"))
  prob_mat <- t(vapply(seq_along(draw_id), function(d) {
    fun_prob(mu[d, ], shape[d], curve_x$beta0, curve_x$beta1)
  }, numeric(nrow(newdat))))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(prob_mat)), all(prob_mat >= 0 & prob_mat <= 1))
  pop_mat <- as.matrix(prob_mat %*% weights)
  dat_draws <- as_tibble(t(pop_mat), .name_repair = "minimal")
  names(dat_draws) <- paste0("draw_", draw_id)
  bind_cols(strategy_groups, dat_draws) %>%
    pivot_longer(starts_with("draw_"), names_to = "draw", values_to = "protection") %>%
    mutate(draw = as.integer(str_remove(draw, "draw_")), curve = curve_x$curve,
           risk10 = curve_x$lambda * (1 - protection),
           disease_free10 = 1 - risk10,
           ve10 = 1 - risk10 / curve_x$risk_ref)
})

sim_comparisons <- sim_draws %>%
  select(-group_id) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = c(protection, risk10, disease_free10, ve10)) %>%
  mutate(diff_bs_pp = 100 * (protection_targeted - protection_baseline),
         diff_bl_pp = 100 * (protection_later - protection_baseline),
         diff_sl_pp = 100 * (protection_targeted - protection_later),
         increasepct_bs = 100 * (protection_targeted / protection_baseline - 1),
         increasepct_bl = 100 * (protection_later / protection_baseline - 1),
         risk_reduction_bs_pct = 100 * (1 - risk10_targeted / risk10_baseline),
         cases_averted_1000 = 1000 * (risk10_baseline - risk10_targeted))

sim_draws %>%
  filter(curve == "published") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = protection, fill = scenario)) + 
  geom_histogram()
```

# Summarise population results

Intervals below propagate antibody-model uncertainty **conditional on each fixed
protection curve**. The marginal confidence limits in the article cannot identify
the joint uncertainty distribution of its coefficients; the sensitivity curves
must not be pooled and labelled a posterior credible interval. Lambda is held fixed
at its estimate. Its reported upper confidence bound exceeds one and is not used
as a valid probability. Protection contrasts do not require lambda; absolute
clinical risks and cases averted do, and retain the trial's exposure assumptions.

```{r}
pop_summ <- sim_comparisons %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(clu, age_ini, delay, time_vl_s1, draw, curve),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(clu, age_ini, delay, time_vl_s1, curve, metric) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(value), med = median(value),
            cilo = quantile(value, .025), ciup = quantile(value, .975), .groups = "drop")
pop_summ
```

# Plots

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
pl_change <- pop_summ %>%
  filter(curve == "published", metric %in% c("increasepct_bs", "increasepct_bl")) %>%
  mutate(scenario = recode(metric, increasepct_bs = "Seasonally targeted delay",
                          increasepct_bl = "Everyone later")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = delay, y = med, color = scenario)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = cilo, ymax = ciup, fill = scenario), alpha = .15, color = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(clu + time_vl_s1 ~ age_ini, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(x = "Delay among targeted children (weeks)",
       y = "Relative change in modelled protection (%)", color = "Scenario", fill = "Scenario") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
pl_change

pl_change <- pop_summ %>%
  filter(curve == "published", metric %in% c("diff_bs_pp", "diff_bl_pp")) %>%
  filter(time_vl_s1 == 42) %>%
  mutate(scenario = recode(metric, diff_bs_pp = "Seasonally targeted delay",
                          diff_bl_pp = "Everyone later")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = delay, y = med, color = scenario)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = cilo, ymax = ciup, fill = scenario), alpha = .15, color = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(clu ~ age_ini, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(x = "Delay among targeted children (weeks)",
       y = "Relative change in modelled protection (%)", color = "Scenario", fill = "Scenario") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
pl_change


pl_sensitivity <- pop_summ %>%
  filter(metric == "diff_bs_pp") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = delay, y = med, color = curve)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey") + geom_line() +
  facet_grid(clu + time_vl_s1 ~ age_ini, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(x = "Delay among targeted children (weeks)",
       y = "Targeted minus early protection (percentage points)") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
pl_sensitivity
```

# Save results

```{r}
saveRDS(sim_draws, glue("{dir_res}/vzv_continuous_population_draws.rds"))
saveRDS(sim_comparisons, glue("{dir_res}/vzv_continuous_comparison_draws.rds"))
saveRDS(pop_summ, glue("{dir_res}/vzv_continuous_population_summary.rds"))
write_csv(pop_summ, glue("{dir_res}/vzv_continuous_population_summary.csv"))
saveRDS(list(curve_ref = curve_ref, curve_scenarios = curve_scenarios,
             dat_cov = dat_cov, dat_phase = dat_phase, draw_id = draw_id,
             antibody_units = antibody_units, assay_scale_confirmed = assay_scale_confirmed,
             check_grid = check_grid, session = sessionInfo()),
        glue("{dir_res}/vzv_continuous_settings.rds"))
ggsave(glue("{dir_res}/vzv_continuous_relative_change.pdf"), pl_change, width = 10, height = 7)
ggsave(glue("{dir_res}/vzv_continuous_curve_sensitivity.pdf"), pl_sensitivity, width = 10, height = 7)
```

# Notes

The paper's antibody marker did not fully explain vaccination effects. Applying this
curve to different schedules, ages, populations, and vaccine-concentration profiles
is a sensitivity analysis requiring transportability assumptions. Changing the
sampling time to 42 days aligns one measurement convention, not the entire trial.
Antibody concentrations outside the trial's observed range extrapolate the curve.
The analysis does not include infections during the delay, waning, transmission,
or differences in exposure between regions. Disease-free probability and VE must
not be presented as measured seroprotection.
